body.statement:
In the multihomogeneous system used by \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\), the query component has at most \(n-1\) nonempty child blocks and its binary-factor graph is simple. For a simple graph on at most two blocks every prescribed-indegree coefficient is at most \(1\); on at most three blocks it is at most \(2\); and on at most four blocks it is at most \(4\), with
\[
 [X_1X_2X_3^2X_4^2]\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq4}(X_i+X_j)=4.
\]
If \(n=5\) and \(|D\setminus T|\leq1\), the coefficient is at most \(3\). Hence every finite queried-coordinate degree satisfies
\[
 d_e(G)\leq1\quad(n=3),\qquad
 d_e(G)\leq2\quad(n=4),\qquad
 d_e(G)\leq3\quad(n=5,\ |D\setminus T|\leq1),
\]
and \(d_e(G)\leq4\) when \(n=5\).
body.proof_tex:
For a finite simple graph \(H=(W,E_H)\) and a vector \(r=(r_v:v\in W)\) of nonnegative integers, define
\[
 c_H(r)=
 \left[\prod_{v\in W}X_v^{r_v}\right]
 \prod_{\{u,v\}\in E_H}(X_u+X_v).
\tag{15}
\]
Choosing \(X_v\) from the factor belonging to \(\{u,v\}\) is equivalent to orienting that edge toward \(v\).  Hence \(c_H(r)\) is exactly the number of orientations of \(H\) with indegree vector \(r\), and in particular
\[
 c_H(r)=0\quad\hbox{unless}\quad
 \sum_{v\in W}r_v=|E_H|,
 \qquad 0\leq r_v\leq\deg_H(v).
\tag{16}
\]

If \(|W|\leq2\), simplicity leaves at most one edge, whose direction is fixed by \(r\); thus \(c_H(r)\leq1\).  If \(|W|\leq3\) and \(H\) is a forest, two orientations with the same indegrees would have a nonempty balanced symmetric difference.  Following an entering edge by a leaving edge in that difference would produce a cycle, contradicting that \(H\) is a forest.  Thus the count is at most one.  The only remaining graph is a triangle.  Its two cyclic orientations both have indegree vector \((1,1,1)\), while each transitive orientation is uniquely determined by its labeled permutation of \((0,1,2)\).  Therefore
\[
 \max_{|W|\leq3,r}c_H(r)=2.
\tag{17}
\]

Suppose next that \(|W|\leq4\).  When \(|E_H|\leq4\), every component is a tree except possibly one unicyclic component: two independent cycles in a simple graph require either at least five edges on four vertices or more than four vertices.  Given an indegree vector, the direction of the edge at a leaf is forced; deleting leaves iteratively fixes every edge outside the unique cycle.  Two orientations of a cycle with the same residual indegrees can differ only on the entire cycle, giving at most its two cyclic orientations.  Componentwise,
\[
 c_H(r)\leq2\qquad(|W|\leq4, |E_H|\leq4).
\tag{18}
\]

With five edges the only possibility is \(H=K_4\setminus\{\{1,2\}\}\).  For
\[
 P=(X_1+X_3)(X_1+X_4)(X_2+X_3)(X_2+X_4)(X_3+X_4),
\]
choosing the number \(a\) of \(X_1\)-terms in the first two factors and the number \(b\) of \(X_2\)-terms in the next two factors, then collecting the two choices in the last factor, gives the exact coefficient maxima
\[
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
  &b=0&b=1&b=2\\ \hline
 a=0&1&2&1\\
 a=1&2&3&2\\
 a=2&1&2&1.
 \end{array}
\tag{19}
\]
Thus every five-edge coefficient is at most three.  If all four block capacities are positive, (16) forces a permutation of \((2,1,1,1)\); (19) gives coefficient three when the exponent two is at vertex \(3\) or \(4\), and coefficient two when it is at vertex \(1\) or \(2\).

With six edges one has \(H=K_4\).  Up to sorting, the only exponent vectors satisfying (16) and \(0\leq r_v\leq3\) are
\[
 (0,0,3,3),\quad(0,1,2,3),\quad(0,2,2,2),
 \quad(1,1,1,3),\quad(1,1,2,2).
\tag{20}
\]
The first coefficient is zero because the edge joining the two zero-exponent vertices has no permissible endpoint.  A labeled vector of type \((0,1,2,3)\) forces the unique transitive orientation.  In types \((0,2,2,2)\) and \((1,1,1,3)\), the edges at the extreme vertex are forced and the remaining triangle has its two cyclic orientations.  For \(r=(1,1,2,2)\), condition on the factor \(X_1+X_2\).  If it contributes \(X_1\), the factors on edges \(13\) and \(14\) must contribute \(X_3X_4\), and the remaining triangle on \(2,3,4\) has two cyclic choices.  The choice \(X_2\) is symmetric.  Therefore
\[
 [X_1X_2X_3^2X_4^2]
 \prod_{1\leq i<j\leq4}(X_i+X_j)=2+2=4,
\tag{21}
\]
and (18)--(21) prove that four is the maximum on four blocks.

We connect these counts to the SEM system.  In the square subsystem used in \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\), variables are partitioned by child vertex.  The root of \(T\) has a directed path in \(T\) to every other vertex; an additional arrow into that root would therefore create a directed cycle and is excluded by acyclicity.  Thus the root block is empty and there are at most \(n-1\) nonempty child blocks.  The displayed formula for \(F_{ij}\) has degree at most one in the block for child \(i\), at most one in the block for child \(j\), and zero in every other child block.  An unordered pair \(\{i,j\}\) supplies at most the one residual \(F_{ij}\); hence the binary-factor graph is simple.  By \(\mathrm{lem:multihomogeneous\mbox{-}bezout\mbox{-}isolated\mbox{-}bound}\), its prescribed multidegree coefficient is the orientation count (15).  Equations (17) and (21), together with the two-block argument, yield
\[
 d_e(G)\leq1\quad(n=3),\qquad
 d_e(G)\leq2\quad(n=4),\qquad
 d_e(G)\leq4\quad(n=5)
\tag{22}
\]
whenever the queried coordinate is algebraic.

Finally suppose \(n=5\) and \(|D\setminus T|\leq1\).  Then \(|D|\leq4+1=5\), so a selected square subsystem has at most five equations and, after its unary factors are removed, at most five binary factors.  Four or fewer binary factors are covered by (18) and give coefficient at most two.  Five binary factors force four nonempty blocks and the graph \(K_4\setminus e\); there is then no unary factor, the four positive block sizes sum to five, and hence their capacity vector is a permutation of \((2,1,1,1)\).  Equation (19) bounds its coefficient by three.  Therefore
\[
 d_e(G)\leq3\qquad(n=5, |D\setminus T|\leq1),
\tag{23}
\]
which proves every assertion.
